claims.scope: task-221 made execute_intent roll back a failed multi-step plan with one system.undo per applied step. That undo is unconditional ('rewind the most recent editable transaction'), so under a concurrent interleaving it rewinds a FOREIGN actor's committed edit and leaves the spine's own half-applied step in place: silent data corruption. Also unaddressed: duplicate delivery re-applies the plan (forward commands carry no idempotency key), a rollback that cannot complete still leaves artifact nodes in the graph, and a crash between the bus commit and the graph node write leaves an unreachable artifact. Fix (spine-only, no bus change; studio/ is not owned): bind each step to its committed transaction_id, on rollback only undo while the most-recent transaction is one the run owns (else refuse with a typed error), retract artifact nodes even on a partial rollback, bind an idempotency key per (intent, step) so a duplicate delivery returns the original result.
acceptance_criteria: a concurrent foreign edit interleaved between a step commit and a later step failure survives the rollback (only the run's own step is undone)
if the run cannot undo its own step because a foreign transaction is latest, the rollback fails closed with SpineRollbackError rather than editing foreign work
a duplicate delivery of the same intent is idempotent: identical state_hash and no second marker
a partial rollback failure still retracts every artifact node the failed run wrote (no orphan artifact/evidence node)
a successful multi-step run is unchanged (no regression)
mutations that (a) drop the transaction-identity check, (b) drop the per-step idempotency key turn the suite RED

claims.title: system.undo must be addressable by transaction identity, not just 'the newest'
claims.title_fa: system.undo باید با هویت تراکنش آدرس‌پذیر باشد، نه فقط «آخرین»
claims.scope: task-221/task-222 finding. ROOT CAUSE: _system_undo in src/nexus_ai_agent/creative/studio/capabilities.py selects the most recent editable transaction globally and restores its full-state snapshot; it has no transaction-identity parameter. task-222 made the SPINE rollback fail closed rather than corrupt a foreign edit, but the bus primitive itself is still globally unsafe for concurrent actors. Because snapshots are full project state, rewinding a non-newest transaction while newer ones stand is not sound, so a correct root fix is a design choice: (A) add an optional transaction_id to system.undo that only rewinds when it is the newest (spine then addresses its own txn, no behavior change when absent); (B) staged command DAG + single commit (no rollback needed); (C) explicit compensating saga per capability. Evaluate with the evidence rules; do NOT pick the smallest diff if it leaves the race.

claims.scope: Found by task-223 while auditing the final PR#128 CI head: python-parity (3.12) failed with sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked on PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL (run 36816623063 job 110223040499) in test_r_f28_concurrent_identical_learns_collapse_into_one; the 3.10/3.11 legs and the local full suite (2988 passed) were green, so it is intermittent and contention-dependent. Owner: storage-observability zone (unclaimed). Local repro attempt: 12 concurrent create_all_tables on a fresh path (single loop) did NOT reproduce the WAL lock (only the already-retried create_all race fired); the lock needs a concurrent writer holding a transaction at first-use init, which the CI test that failed supplies. No speculative fix attempted out of zone without a deterministic RED test.
acceptance_criteria: PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL under concurrent first use never raises 'database is locked' (busy_timeout + bounded retry on the one-time pragma)

claims.note: RED reproduced deterministically (both pre-fix tests fail in ~1.3s): a raw sqlite3 connection holding BEGIN IMMEDIATE makes a bare PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL raise 'database is locked'. Mutation evidence (PYTHONPATH forced to the mutant): M1 = bare pragma, timeout kept -> 3 failed (busy timeout alone does NOT cover the WAL transition); M2 = retry kept, timeout removed -> 3 passed (the retry is load-bearing).
